channels.title: Channels
channels.descriptionOrganization: Chat channels and webhooks the alerts of the organization and its projects can post to.
channels.descriptionProject: Channels only this project's alerts can use.
channels.privacyNotice: A channel is read by people who may have no GitOps account or permissions. The channel URL is stored encrypted and never shown in full again.
channels.testFailed: The test message could not be sent ({reason}).
channels.confirmDelete: Delete this channel? Alerts using it will stop posting to it.
channels.name: Name
channels.newDestination: New URL (empty keeps the current one)
channels.inheritedDescription: This project's alerts can also use these channels. They are managed from the organization settings.
channels.noTypes: No channel type is available yet.

testMessage.title: GitOps test message for {channel}
testMessage.summary: This channel will get the alerts of {where}.

channels.autoDisabled: Disabled after {failures} failed deliveries in a row
channels.confirmRotate: A new secret will be generated. For the next 24 hours deliveries are signed with both the new and the current secret, so the receiver can switch over; after that only the new one is valid.
channels.secretDescription: Copy it now and configure it in the receiver: it will not be shown again. Each delivery carries an X-GitOps-Signature header made with it.
channels.webhookHelp: Any public https URL. GitOps signs each request with HMAC-SHA256 and never follows redirects.
channels.slackHelp: Slack Incoming Webhook URL (https://hooks.slack.com/services/…). The webhook decides the Slack channel: create one per channel in your Slack app, under "Incoming Webhooks".
channels.localeHelp: Messages to this channel (event, fields and button) are written in this language.
channels.slackConnectDescription: Pick the workspace and the channel in Slack: GitOps names the channel and saves its webhook, nothing to copy.
channels.slackManual: or paste an Incoming Webhook URL
channels.slackSetupHint: Add to Slack (pick the channel in Slack, no URL to copy) is not set up yet.
channels.slackAppRemoveConfirm: /gitops stops working in that workspace until it is installed again. Channels already connected keep posting; to revoke them, remove the app in Slack.

slackApp.notInstalled: This Slack workspace is not connected to GitOps. An organization admin has to click *Install in Slack* in GitOps (Settings → Alerts → Settings → Channels).
slackApp.help:
*GitOps commands*
• `/gitops login`: link your Slack user to your GitOps account (once).
• `/gitops channel`: connect a Slack channel to the organization's alerts.
• `/gitops status`: linked organization, your account and the connected channels.
slackApp.notLinked: Link your GitOps account first with `/gitops login`.
slackApp.forbidden: Your GitOps account is not allowed to create channels in this organization.
slackApp.failed: GitOps could not complete the action ({code}).
slackApp.linkExpires: This link is only for you and expires in 10 minutes.

login.prompt: Open GitOps to link your Slack user to your account (sign in with your password or with Google).

status.noChannels: No Slack channels connected yet (`/gitops channel`).

channel.name: Name

channel.pick: Last step: pick the Slack channel for *{name}*. Slack opens in the browser with your channels; once you allow it, GitOps saves the configuration and posts a test message to the channel.
